facts.statement: The genus Staurikosaurus was described by Edwin Harris Colbert in 1970.

facts.statement: The species name of the dinosaur is pricei.
facts.quote: species: pricei

facts.statement: Teyuwasu barberenai was synonymized with Staurikosaurus pricei in 1999.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Teyuwasu barberenai Kischlat, 1999

facts.statement: Colbert described Staurikosaurus as a small, agile, bipedal predator.
facts.quote: Colbert (1970) described Staurikosaurus as a small and agile, bipedal predator.

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus lived approximately 225 million years ago during the late-Carnian and early-Norian stages of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus lived during the late-Carnian and early-Norian stage, of the Late Triassic, approximately 225 million years ago

facts.statement: The length of Staurikosaurus is measured at 2.2 to 2.25 meters.
facts.quote: Its length is measured at 2.2 - 2.25 m long

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Staurikosaurus at 2.1 meters and its body mass at 12 kilograms.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul presented a lower length estimate of 2.1 m and a body mass estimate of 12 kg.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Staurikosaurus has long but relatively slender limb bones.
facts.quote: The type specimen has long but relatively slender limb bones.

facts.statement: The available teeth of Staurikosaurus suggest a carnivorous diet.
facts.quote: The available teeth for Staurikosaurus bear a morphology that strongly suggests a carnivorous diet.

facts.statement: The teeth of Staurikosaurus are serrated, laterally compressed, and curved backward toward the throat.
facts.quote: The teeth are all serrated, laterally compressed, and caudally curved

facts.statement: The tail of Staurikosaurus was relatively long, containing more than 40 vertebrae.
facts.quote: The tail of Staurikosaurus was relatively long (with more than 40 vertebrae) compared to the rest of its body

facts.statement: Ostrom suggested that the stiffened tail of Staurikosaurus served as a dynamic stabilizer for leaping and running.
facts.quote: Ostrom (1969a) considered this adaptation to serve as a dynamic stabilizer facilitating the animal's leaping and running.

facts.statement: The first known specimen of Staurikosaurus (MCZ 1669) was found at the Jazigo Cinco site in the Santa Maria Formation, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
facts.quote: The first known specimen of Staurikosaurus (MCZ 1669) was recovered from the Paleontological Site Jazigo Cinco of the Santa Maria Formation, Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil.

facts.statement: The specific name pricei honors Llewellyn Ivor Price, who discovered the dinosaur in 1936.
facts.quote: The specific name honors the Brazilian paleontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price, who discovered it in 1936.

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus is considered more primitive than other dinosaurs because it has only two sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus is considered to be more primitive than any other dinosaur because only two sacral vertebrae are present

facts.statement: Garcia et al. (2019) referred the holotype of Teyuwasu barberenai as a second specimen of Staurikosaurus pricei.
facts.quote: Garcia et al. (2019) referred the holotype of Teyuwasu barberenai as a second specimen of Staurikosaurus pricei

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus is classified within the clade Herrerasauridae according to the scientific consensus established since 1994.
facts.quote: All major phylogenetic analyses since 1994 have assigned Staurikosaurus to the clade Herrerasauridae, which is the current scientific consensus on classification of this genus.

facts.statement: Colbert originally misclassified Staurikosaurus in the defunct family Palaeosauriscidae before it was moved to Herrerasauridae.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus was originally incorrectly assigned by Colbert to Palaeosauriscidae, a defunct family based largely on Efraasia, a prosauropod dinosaur.

facts.statement: The genus Staurikosaurus was named by Colbert in 1970.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Colbert, 1970

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 225 million years ago in the Carnian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 225 millones de años, en el Carniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus is considered one of the oldest known dinosaurs, alongside Herrerasaurus, Panphagia, and Eoraptor.
facts.quote: Es uno de los dinosaurios más antiguos conocidos, junto a Herrerasaurus, Panphagia y Eoraptor.

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus was a small, active bipedal predator that hunted small to medium-sized terrestrial vertebrates including cynodonts, rhynchosaurs, and herbivorous synapsids.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus was a small but active bipedal predator, that preyed on small and medium-sized terrestrial vertebrates such as cynodonts, rhynchosaurs, and herbivorous synapsids.

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus is considerably smaller than Herrerasaurus, with a femur length of 23 cm compared to 47 cm.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus differs from Herrerasaurus because of its considerably smaller size (femur length of 23 cm vs. 47 cm).

facts.statement: The mandible of Staurikosaurus suggests it had a sliding joint allowing the jaw to move backwards, forwards, up, and down.
facts.quote: The mandible of Staurikosaurus suggests that a sliding joint in the jaw allowed it to move backwards and forwards, as well as up and down.

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus likely processed smaller prey by working it backwards toward its throat using small, backwards-curving teeth.
facts.quote: Smaller prey could be worked backwards towards Staurikosauruss throat, aided along by its small, backwards-curving teeth.

facts.statement: The environment where Staurikosaurus lived was arid to semi-arid, featuring seed ferns, ferns, cycads, and conifers.
facts.quote: The region where Staurikosaurus lived was arid to semi-arid, characterized by a mix of seed ferns, ferns, cycads, and conifers.

facts.statement: Sereno et al. (1993) concluded that Staurikosaurus was not a theropod but a basal saurischian outside the Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha clades.
facts.quote: Sereno et al. (1993) concluded that Staurikosaurus was not a theropod and considered it a basal saurischian outside Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha.

facts.statement: The dinosauriform Teyuwasu barberenai has been controversially proposed as a synonym of Staurikosaurus pricei based on shared osteological features.
facts.quote: The controversial dinosauriform "Teyuwasu barberenai" was recently considered a synonym of Staurikosaurus pricei.

facts.statement: Further investigation is required to confirm or reject the proposed synonymy between Teyuwasu barberenai and Staurikosaurus pricei.
facts.quote: Therefore, further investigations are needed in order to whether confirm or not the synonymy between "Teyuwasu barberenai" and Staurikosaurus pricei.

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus was the first known dinosaur discovered in Brazil, found by paleontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price in 1936.
facts.quote: Es el primer dinosaurio conocido de Brasil y fue descubierto por el paleontólogo Llewellyn Ivor Price en 1936

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus lived during the late Carnian and early Norian stages of the Late Triassic, approximately 225 million years ago.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus vivió durante la etapa tardía del Carniense y principios del Noriense, del Triásico tardío, hace aproximadamente 225 millones de años

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus measured 2.25 meters in length, 80 centimeters in height, and weighed 30 kilograms.
facts.quote: Con 2,25 metros de largo, 80 centímetros de alto y un peso de 30 kilogramos

facts.statement: The fossil record of Staurikosaurus is very incomplete, consisting mainly of the spine, legs, and large lower jaw.
facts.quote: Existe registro muy incompleto de fósiles de Staurikosaurus, consiste en la mayor parte de la espina dorsal, piernas y la gran mandíbula inferior

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus is generally depicted with five toes on its feet and five fingers on its hands, traits of an unspecialized dinosaur.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus se representa generalmente con cinco dedos del pie y cinco dedos en las manos, características de un dinosaurio no especializado

facts.statement: In 1969, Ostrom suggested that Staurikosaurus's tail adaptation functioned as a dynamic stabilizer that facilitated jumping and running.
facts.quote: Ostrom en 1969 consideró que esta adaptación funcionaba como un estabilizador dinámico que facilitaba los saltos y las carreras del animal

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus had a relatively long tail with more than 40 vertebrae.
facts.quote: La cola del Staurikosaurus era relativamente larga, con más de 40 vértebras

facts.statement: The available teeth of Staurikosaurus have a morphology that strongly suggests a carnivorous diet.
facts.quote: Los dientes disponibles para Staurikosaurus tienen una morfología que sugiere fuertemente una dieta carnívora

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus had a jaw almost as long as its femur.
facts.quote: Una mandíbula casi tan larga como el fémur

facts.statement: The dentary of Staurikosaurus contained 13 to 14 teeth.
facts.quote: con 13 a 14 dientes

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus had a vertebral column with 9 to 10 cervical vertebrae, 15 dorsal vertebrae, 2 sacral vertebrae, and more than 40 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Una columna vertebral con 9 a 10 vértebras cervicales, 15 dorsales, 2 sacras y más de 40 caudales

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus is considered more primitive than any other dinosaur because it possesses only two sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Se considera que Staurikosaurus es más primitivo que cualquier otro dinosaurio porque solo están presentes dos vértebras sacras

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus was found in the city of Santa Maria, in the state of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
facts.quote: Fue hallado en la ciudad de Santa Maria, en el estado de Río Grande do Sul, en Brasil

facts.statement: The fossils were found at the Jazigo Cinco Paleontological Site in the Santa Maria Formation.
facts.quote: Se encontró en Sitio Paleontológico Jazigo Cinco de la Formación Santa María

facts.statement: The species name pricei honors the Brazilian paleontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price, who extracted the fossil.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie hace referencia al paleontólogo brasileño Llewellyn Ivor Price, quien extrajera el fósil

facts.statement: In 2019, García et al. referred the holotype of Teyuwasu barberenai as a second specimen of Staurikosaurus pricei.
facts.quote: García et al. en 2019 refirieron el holotipo de Teyuwasu barberenai como un segundo espécimen de Staurikosaurus pricei

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus was initially considered a basal prosauropod but was quickly reclassified as a theropod.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus fue considerado en un principio como un prosaurópodo basal, rápidamente esto fue dejado de lado y colocado dentro de los terópodos

facts.statement: In 1977, Galtón created the unique family Staurikosauridae for Staurikosaurus.
facts.quote: Galtón en 1977 llamada Staurikosauridae

facts.statement: In 1993, Sereno and Novas placed Staurikosaurus within the family Herrerasauridae.
facts.quote: Luego en 1993 Sereno y Novas lo colocan dentro de Herrerasauridae

facts.statement: Benedetto in 1973 and Galton in 1985 were the first to recognize that Staurikosaurus and Herrerasaurus were more closely related to each other than to sauropodomorphs or avemetatarsalians.
facts.quote: Mortimer señala que Benedetto en 1973 y Galton en 1985 fueron los primeros en reconocer que Staurikosaurus y Herrerasaurus estaban más estrechamente relacionados entre sí

facts.statement: Colbert originally and incorrectly assigned Staurikosaurus to the family Palaeosauriscidae.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus fue originalmente asignado incorrectamente por Colbert a Palaeosauriscidae

facts.statement: Since 1994, major phylogenetic analyses have assigned Staurikosaurus to the clade Herrerasauridae, which is the current scientific consensus.
facts.quote: Todos los principales análisis filogenéticos desde 1994 han asignado a Staurikosaurus al clado Herrerasauridae, que es el consenso científico actual

facts.statement: The controversial dinosaur Teyuwasu barberenai was recently considered a synonym of Staurikosaurus pricei.
facts.quote: El controvertido dinosaurio Teyuwasu barberenai fue considerado recientemente como sinónimo de Staurikosaurus pricei

facts.statement: Two subsequent articles have questioned the association between Teyuwasu and Staurikosaurus.

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus lived during the Carnian stage of the Triassic, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.quote: Staurikosaurus difiere de Herrerasaurus debido a su tamaño considerablemente más pequeño, su longitud del fémur es de 23 centímetros frente a 47 centímetros

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus was a small but active bipedal predator that fed on small to medium-sized terrestrial vertebrates such as cynodonts, rincosaurs, and herbivorous synapsids.

facts.statement: The jaw of Staurikosaurus suggests it had a sliding joint that allowed movement forward and backward, as well as up and down.
facts.quote: La mandíbula de Staurikosaurus sugiere que una articulación deslizante en la mandíbula le permitía moverse hacia adelante y hacia atrás, así como hacia arriba y hacia abajo

facts.statement: Smaller prey could be moved backward toward Staurikosaurus's throat with the help of its small, backward-curving teeth.
facts.quote: Las presas más pequeñas podían moverse hacia atrás, hacia la garganta de Staurikosaurus, con la ayuda de sus pequeños dientes curvados hacia atrás

facts.statement: Some authors have questioned the presence of an intramandibular joint in Staurikosaurus due to poor preservation of the holotype.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, algunos autores cuestionaron la presencia de una articulación intramandibular en Staurikosaurus, debido a la mala conservación del holotipo

facts.statement: Staurikosaurus coexisted with large rauisuchian archosaurs like Rauisuchus, which were the main carnivores in its ecosystem.
facts.quote: Staurikosaurus coexistió con grandes arcosaurios rauisuquios como Rauisuchus, que eran los principales carnívoros en su ecosistema

facts.statement: U-Pb dating found the Santa Maria Formation to be about 233.23 million years old, placing it 1.5 million years before the Ischigualasto Formation.
facts.quote: Una datación U-Pb, desintegración del uranio, encontró que la Formación Santa María databa de hace unos 233,23 millones de años, lo que la sitúa 1,5 millones de años antes que la Formación Ischigualasto

facts.statement: Research by Sues et al. in 2011 supports that Staurikosaurus and the related genus Herrerasaurus are theropods that evolved after the sauropod line separated from Theropoda.
facts.quote: Investigaciones posteriores de Sues et al. en 2011 apoya que Staurikosaurus y el género relacionado Herrerasaurus son terópodos y evolucionaron después de que la línea de saurópodos se separó de Theropoda

facts.quote: Sereno et al. en 1993 concluyó que Staurikosaurus no era un terópodo y lo consideró un saurisquio basal fuera de Theropoda y Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: In 2010, Alcober and Martínez concluded that Staurikosaurus and Sanjuansaurus are closely related based on similarities in their pubis and tibia.
facts.quote: Alcober y Martínez en 2010 concluyeron que Staurikosaurus y Sanjuansaurus están estrechamente relacionados con base en similitudes en su pubis y tibia
